title: Statics and Torque
learning_objectives: State the first condition for equilibrium and use it to solve for unknown forces.
State the second condition for equilibrium and compute a moment.
Explain the stability of a body from the position of its centre of gravity.

sections.title: Introduction to Statics and Torque
objectives: Describe what statics studies and why the turning effect of a force matters.

misconceptions.claim: Statics is the study of moving objects.
misconceptions.correction: It is the study of objects at rest, and of the forces and moments that keep them there.

summary: Statics is the study of equilibrium.
A moment is the turning effect of a force about a pivot.
Two conditions decide whether a body is in equilibrium.
sections.no_worked_example_reason: The source carries no worked example for this section and no solved exercise to promote, so the practice is left to the exercises themselves.

sections.title: The First Condition for Equilibrium
objectives: Use the first condition for equilibrium, that the net force is zero.

misconceptions.claim: A body at rest has no forces acting on it.
misconceptions.correction: It has forces acting on it that balance, so the net force is zero.

summary: The first condition is that the vector sum of the forces is zero.
Balanced forces need not be equal pairs, they must sum to zero in every direction.
The forces need not act at the same point for this condition.
sections.no_worked_example_reason: The source carries no worked example for this section and no solved exercise to promote, so the practice is left to the exercises themselves.

sections.title: The Second Condition for Equilibrium
objectives: Use the second condition for equilibrium, that the net moment is zero.

misconceptions.claim: If the forces balance, the body is in equilibrium.
misconceptions.correction: Only if the forces balance and the turning effects balance as well. A couple is a pair of forces that turn a body without changing its motion.

summary: The second condition is that the net moment about any pivot is zero.
A moment is force times the perpendicular distance from the pivot.
A couple turns a body and gives it no net force.

sections.title: Stability
objectives: Explain stability from the position of the centre of gravity relative to the base of support.

misconceptions.claim: A body is stable when its centre of gravity is high.
misconceptions.correction: It is stable when the centre of gravity is low, or when it lies over the base of support, so a small tilt raises it.

summary: Stable, unstable and neutral depend on the centre of gravity and the base of support.
Tilting a stable body raises its centre of gravity, so it falls back.
A hanging object is stable because its centre of gravity is below the pivot.

sections.title: Applications of Statics, Including Problem-Solving Strategies
objectives: Set up a statics problem by drawing the free-body diagram before writing any equation.

misconceptions.claim: You can write the equilibrium equations straight away.
misconceptions.correction: You draw the free-body diagram first, choose a pivot, and only then write the equations.

summary: Always draw the free-body diagram first.
Choose a pivot that removes an unknown force where you can.
Solve the force equations and the moment equations together.

sections.title: Simple Machines
objectives: Explain the mechanical advantage of a simple machine and compute it from the forces.

misconceptions.claim: A machine multiplies the force applied.
misconceptions.correction: It trades force for distance, so it multiplies the force only when it moves the load less far, and the mechanical advantage says by how much.

summary: The mechanical advantage is the load over the effort.
No machine is better than the effort: the work in equals the work out.
Machines save force or save distance, never both.

conditions.text: The vector sum of the forces on the body is zero.
With d the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of the force.
The net moment about the pivot is zero.
For an ideal machine, where the work in equals the work out.

definition.text: The state of a body at rest or in uniform motion, with the net force and the net moment both zero.
The turning effect of a force about a pivot, equal to the force times the perpendicular distance from the pivot.
A pair of equal and opposite forces whose lines of action are apart, which turns a body without moving its centre.
The point at which the whole weight of a body can be treated as acting.
The factor by which a machine multiplies the effort, equal to the load over the effort.

exam_traps.subject: physics
exam_traps.misconception: The normal force on a body resting on a floor is half its weight.
exam_traps.correction: The floor pushes up with a force equal to the weight, so the normal force is the whole weight.
exam_traps.signal: Our own question offers half the weight as an option.

exam_traps.subject: physics
exam_traps.misconception: The angle between the force and the arm does not change the moment.
exam_traps.correction: Only the component of the force perpendicular to the arm turns the body, so the moment is F d sin(theta).
exam_traps.signal: Our own question offers the moment with the angle ignored.

exam_traps.subject: physics
exam_traps.misconception: A body is stable when its centre of gravity is high.
exam_traps.correction: A body is stable when a small tilt raises its centre of gravity, so a low centre of gravity inside a wide base is stable.
exam_traps.signal: Our own question offers the high centre of gravity case.

exam_traps.subject: physics
exam_traps.misconception: The output work of a machine is the input work divided by the efficiency.
exam_traps.correction: The output work is the input work multiplied by the efficiency, and the mechanical advantage is the load over the effort.
exam_traps.signal: The paper offers the value from dividing, and the answer is the value from multiplying.

exam_traps.subject: physics
exam_traps.misconception: The normal force on a body resting on a floor is a tenth of its weight.
exam_traps.correction: It is the whole weight. The floor pushes up with exactly the force the weight pushes down.
exam_traps.signal: Our own question offers the value with the mass alone.

exam_traps.subject: physics
exam_traps.misconception: The moment of a force is the force divided by the distance from the pivot.
exam_traps.correction: The moment is the force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the pivot.
exam_traps.signal: Our own question offers the force divided by the distance as an option.

exam_traps.subject: physics
exam_traps.misconception: A narrow base makes a body stable.
exam_traps.correction: A narrow base makes a body unstable. A body is stable when a small tilt raises its centre of gravity.
exam_traps.signal: Our own question offers the narrow base as the stable case.

exam_traps.subject: physics
exam_traps.misconception: The mechanical advantage of a machine includes its efficiency.
exam_traps.correction: The mechanical advantage is the load over the effort. The efficiency is a separate ratio, and multiplying the two is not the mechanical advantage.
exam_traps.signal: The paper offers the efficiency times the mechanical advantage, and the answer is the mechanical advantage alone.

exam_recall_checks.subject: physics
exam_recall_checks.stem: A box of mass 20 kg rests on a horizontal floor. What is the normal force on the box? (Take g = 10 m/s2.)
exam_recall_checks.explanation: The floor pushes up with a force equal to the weight, so the normal force is 200 N.
exam_recall_checks.source: authored against the JAMB physics syllabus

exam_recall_checks.subject: physics
exam_recall_checks.stem: A force of 100 N acts at a point 2 m from a pivot, at 30 degrees to the arm. What is the moment about the pivot?
exam_recall_checks.explanation: Only the component perpendicular to the arm turns the body, so the moment is 100 x 2 x sin 30 = 100 N m.
exam_recall_checks.source: authored against the JAMB physics syllabus

exam_recall_checks.subject: physics
exam_recall_checks.stem: A force of 60 N acts at a point 1.5 m from a pivot, perpendicular to the arm. What is the moment about the pivot?
exam_recall_checks.explanation: The moment is the force times the perpendicular distance, so 60 x 1.5 = 90 N m.

exam_recall_checks.subject: physics
exam_recall_checks.stem: A machine has a mechanical advantage of 3 and an efficiency of 50%. What effort is needed to raise a load of 120 N?
exam_recall_checks.explanation: The mechanical advantage is the load over the effort, so the effort is 120/3 = 40 N. The efficiency does not change the mechanical advantage.
